regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; the quality check is less flattering. PMI Composite at 55.9 is services-led — manufacturing PMI at 55.1 recovered from 52.8 but core sector decelerated to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and IIP overall at 8.0% YoY is doing the heavy lifting only because capital goods (16.9% YoY) are running hot. The inversion: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is above the threshold where private capex historically accelerates, but if credit conditions tighten as the deposit gap forces macro-prudential action, that capex impulse stalls before it compounds.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"The headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is a trapdoor — decompose it and the alarm is in fuel at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile), not core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile). That gap matters enormously: fuel inflation is supply-side and imported, which means the RBI cannot cure it with rate hikes without crushing demand unnecessarily. The second-order effect is the one to watch — Brent at $111.7/bbl feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, which leads PPI, which leads core CPI with a two-quarter lag. Core is low today; it may not be by Q1 FY28.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY is a 160 bps divergence that has widened for two consecutive months — the CD ratio at 81% sits at the 73rd historical percentile. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within four quarters, the RBI was forced into emergency tightening. The setup today rhymes, with one difference: NBFC credit is accelerating at 15.8% YoY and services credit at 24.3% YoY, meaning the stress is migrating to the segments least able to absorb a funding shock.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is on extended hold, but the real rate is doing the work the RBI won't. With CPI at 5.54% YoY, the real repo rate is effectively negative — which means monetary policy is still accommodative even as the RBI signals vigilance. The RBI's own inflation forecast has been revised up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%, yet the policy rate hasn't moved. That inconsistency has a cost: INR at 95.24 ₹/USD (89th percentile) is already pricing the credibility gap, and every month of inaction widens the window for a disorderly adjustment.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY rising from 16.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) — this is the most credible signal of a genuine investment upcycle in several quarters. Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY and vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY confirm that financing is flowing into productive assets, not just consumption. The risk: core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) is the canary — if infrastructure output decelerates while capital goods orders are still strong, the pipeline is filling faster than the foundation can support it.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month (73rd percentile) is stable but not accelerating — the prior month was ₹1,99,853 cr / month, so the sequential uptick is modest. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are decelerating (from 16.0% and 26.1% in prior months), while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY bounced sharply — a classic dual-economy signal where mass-market rural demand recovers while urban discretionary softens. The GST number at this level reflects formalization as much as demand; e-way bill velocity and UPI transaction value per user would sharpen the read, but the vehicle data alone suggests the consumption engine is running unevenly across income segments.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"The deposit acceleration masks structural stress: retail deposits are growing, but wholesale funding gaps are widening for smaller banks and NBFCs. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and deposit franchises in metros. Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities — they will face margin compression or forced deleveraging if credit growth stays above 18%. Watch for RBI to signal forbearance on CD ratio limits in next policy review.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; historically, ratios >85% preceded NBFC stress in 2018-19. Current divergence is manageable if deposit growth sustains above 15% YoY.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Capital Goods","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (52nd percentile), up from 16.1% YoY. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile), up from 75.6% — now in the zone where capex typically accelerates. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (50th percentile), a slight deceleration from 5%, but this masks divergence: credit to industry at 18.2% YoY (74th percentile) and credit to agriculture at 17.2% YoY (78th percentile, rising 2 straight months). Vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY (68th percentile, rising 2 straight months).","implication":"Capex is broadening from traditional capital goods into working capital and vehicle financing — a sign of confidence in demand durability. Overweight capital goods manufacturers, auto OEMs, and industrial equipment suppliers. Increase exposure to cement, steel, and logistics. The 77.4% capacity utilisation level historically precedes 12-18 months of sustained capex; this is mid-cycle, not late-cycle.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile is the highest in 3 years; the last time it was this high (2021-22), capex growth sustained at 15%+ for 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Ticket Size Rising","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising 3 consecutive months (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490 cr / month). SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (2nd percentile, but data quality issue noted). SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (89th percentile), up from ₹16.64 lakh cr 3 months ago. Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile), up from ₹29,329 cr / month. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile), offsetting FII outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile).","implication":"Retail is not just entering; average ticket size is rising (SIP AUM +7.3% while accounts flat). Watch for SIP growth to decelerate below 8% YoY as a warning signal.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile are at all-time highs; the last time inflows were this strong (2021), they sustained for 8 quarters before normalising.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, strong-negative signal, score -90), up from 20.05% YoY — a 288 bps jump. Brent crude at $111.7/bbl (down from $116.72/bbl but still elevated, 77th percentile). WTI at $103.27/bbl (84th percentile). Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (52nd percentile), up from 4.83% YoY, driven by food (7.74% YoY, 57th percentile) and fuel. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile, low). RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (53rd percentile).","implication":"Fuel inflation is the tail risk to RBI's rate pause. If Brent stays above $110/bbl and fuel inflation remains >20% YoY for 2 more months, RBI will face pressure to hike despite growth concerns. Hedge long equity positions with short oil futures or long INR calls. Avoid refiners and airlines; they will face margin compression. Overweight energy importers (IT, pharma) that benefit from INR weakness.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest in 5 years; the last time it spiked this high (2022), RBI hiked 190 bps in 4 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry; DXY Stable","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, strong-negative signal, score -100), up from 1% p.a. — rising 2 straight months (0.75%→1%→1.25%). Fed funds at 3.75% p.a. (68th percentile, mild-negative), up from 3.63% p.a. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (63rd percentile), up from 2.25% p.a. US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile, strong-negative, score -80), down from 5.13% yield. DXY at 101.752 (54th percentile, neutral). US PMI Composite at 58.4 index (91st percentile, strong-positive), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"BOJ tightening is the structural headwind to carry trades and EM currencies. Reduce leverage in EM FX; hedge JPY exposure. Overweight USD-earning exporters (IT, pharma). The carry unwind is orderly but will persist — expect INR to trade 95-97 range.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 100th percentile is the highest rate in 17 years; the last time BOJ tightened this aggressively (2006-07), EM currencies fell 15-20% over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens as Carry Unwind Accelerates","data_text":"INR at 95.24 ₹/USD (89th percentile, strong-negative signal, score -78), up from 94.94 ₹/USD. Recent trend: 96.15→97.09→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24 ₹/USD (up 2 of last 5 observations). FII equity net at -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile, mild-negative), a sharp reversal from +₹29,631 cr / month 2 months prior. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) is offsetting FII outflows. US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile) is attracting capital away from EM.","implication":"INR weakness is driven by global carry unwind (BOJ tightening, US Treasury yields elevated) and FII rotation, not India-specific weakness. Underweight import-heavy sectors (autos, capital goods). Hedge INR exposure for corporates with USD liabilities.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness is elevated but not crisis-level; the last time INR was this weak (2022), it fell to 83 ₹/USD before RBI intervention stabilised it.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Surge While Vacancy Stable — GCC Decoupling","data_text":"Bengaluru office rent at ₹163/sqft/mo (95th percentile, strong-positive, score +90), up from ₹148/sqft/mo — a 10.1% jump. Mumbai office rent at ₹156/sqft/mo (59th percentile), up from ₹144/sqft/mo. Office absorption at 24.6 mn sq ft / quarter (18th percentile, mild-negative, score -64), up from 20.8 mn sq ft / quarter, but vacancy at 14.5% (42nd percentile, neutral) — essentially flat. Office vacancy has compressed from 14.7% to 11.4% over 5 quarters, then re-expanded to 14.5%. Nifty IT index flat YoY while Bengaluru rents up 10%.","implication":"Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — not traditional IT services — are the marginal tenant. They are consolidating space (lower absorption, higher rents) while IT services firms are shedding. This decoupling signals a structural shift: GCC capex is resilient, but IT services employment is stalling. Overweight IT infrastructure plays (data centers, commercial REITs like Embassy, Mindspace) and underweight mid-tier IT services firms with high real estate costs. The rent spike in Bengaluru is a leading indicator of GCC expansion; watch for similar moves in Hyderabad and Pune.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Bengaluru office rents at 95th percentile are the highest in 10 years; the last time rents spiked this sharply (2015-16), they sustained for 3 years before normalising, driven by GCC expansion.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Engine Is Misfiring on Two Cylinders

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) and IIP at 8.0% YoY confirm expansion — capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity signal a genuine investment upcycle.
  • But core sector decelerated to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and passenger vehicle sales fell to 7.9% YoY from 16.0% — the goods economy is not keeping pace with the services headline.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY rebounded sharply, suggesting rural mass-market demand is recovering even as urban discretionary softens.
  • GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is stable but sequential momentum is thin — the prior print was ₹1,99,853 cr / month, a 1.8% sequential gain that reflects formalization as much as demand.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY is services-driven and investment-led; the goods economy — core sector, PV sales, CV sales — is decelerating. A growth regime built on two of four cylinders is not the same as broad-based expansion.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a second consecutive print below 4.5% YoY would signal that the investment upcycle is not yet transmitting into output, and GDP quality downgrades follow.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-Acceleration Meets BOJ Tightening — EM Caught in the Crossfire

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile, rising 2 in a row) signals genuine re-acceleration — but US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR is still below trend, and US CPI at 3.72% YoY is rising for the third consecutive month.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising 2 in a row from 0.75%) is the underappreciated tail — every 25 bps of BOJ tightening unwinds yen carry trades that have funded EM equity inflows for a decade.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile) has eased from 5.13% — a 17 bps relief — but remains structurally elevated, keeping the cost of capital for EM borrowers punishing.
  • But Eurozone GDP at 1.2% YoY (rising 2 in a row) and China PMI Composite at 52.1 (recovering from 49.5) suggest the global deceleration narrative is not uniform.

The tension: DM surveys are pricing re-acceleration; DM central banks are still tightening or holding at restrictive levels. The BOJ is the variable the consensus is underweighting — its tightening cycle is at the 100th percentile and has no historical precedent in the carry-trade era.

Bottom line: Hedge EM carry exposure: the next BOJ meeting is the single most important event for India's FII flow trajectory, not the Fed.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds the Market — But Institutional Conviction Has Exited

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile, rising 3 in a row) and DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) are absorbing FII outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) almost exactly.
  • But NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) from ₹3,051 cr / month — the lowest in a decade, signalling that asset managers see no compelling new theme to sell to institutional allocators.
  • Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile) are rising, but MF AUM fell to ₹82.64 lakh cr from ₹87.08 lakh cr — mark-to-market erosion is outpacing fresh flows.
  • INR at 95.24 ₹/USD (89th percentile) reflects the net FII outflow pressure; DXY at 101.8 (54th percentile, neutral) means the INR weakness is India-specific, not a broad dollar story.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are structurally robust and mechanically absorbing FII selling — but NFO collapse and AUM erosion signal that the market is being held up by inertia, not conviction. That is a fragile equilibrium.

Bottom line: Watch weekly FII equity net: if outflows sustain above ₹15,000 cr / week for two more weeks, DII absorption capacity will be tested and Nifty 50 support at 22,000 becomes the line.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand and GCC Rents Diverge From Equity REIT Pricing

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (up 8 pp vs prior period), with 25% share within premium/luxury; remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY) provide the funding runway.
  • Bengaluru office rent at ₹163/sqft/mo (95th percentile, up 10.1% from ₹148/sqft/mo) with GCCs at 42% of occupier mix — but office REITs are pricing the opposite: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹422), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹488).
  • Hyderabad leads residential momentum — sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, only 28 months unsold inventory — while NCR sales turned negative at -1% YoY despite prices up 12% YoY.
  • But Nifty 50 at 22,600 (73rd percentile, down 6 sessions in a row) and Bank Nifty at 54,287 (89th percentile) are under pressure — India VIX at 16.86 (rising 4 of last 5 sessions) signals hedging demand is building.

The tension: Physical office rents and NRI residential demand are at multi-year highs; listed REITs and equities are falling. Either the physical market is pricing a GCC demand story that listed instruments haven't caught up to, or REIT unit prices are correctly discounting a vacancy re-expansion from 11.4% back toward 14.5%.

Bottom line: Overweight physical Bengaluru and Hyderabad residential (NRI + GCC demand structural); avoid listed office REITs until vacancy stabilises below 13% vacant for two consecutive quarters.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fuses, One Detonator — BOJ Is Lighting the Match

The facts:

  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) unwinding yen carry — FII equity outflows already at ₹49,935 cr / month; a further 25 bps BOJ hike could accelerate outflows beyond DII absorption capacity.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $111.7/bbl — every $10/bbl adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widening CAD by ~40 bps and putting INR at 95.24 ₹/USD under further pressure.
  • CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — NBFC credit at 15.8% YoY accelerating into a tightening funding environment is the systemic stress point.
  • But US PMI at 58.4 (91st percentile) re-accelerating while US CPI rises to 3.72% YoY — any Fed pivot reversal would compound the EM outflow and INR depreciation simultaneously.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the danger is sequencing — BOJ hike triggers carry unwind, FII outflows accelerate, INR depreciates, imported fuel inflation widens, RBI cannot cut, credit conditions tighten, NBFC funding stress surfaces. The chain is plausible within two quarters.

Bottom line: Watch the BOJ policy meeting: a rate hold at 1.25% p.a. stabilises the carry trade and buys India 60–90 days; a hike to 1.50% p.a. triggers the sequence above and makes INR 97–98 ₹/USD the base case.

"}
